DeviceCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Insert an effect in a track's chain. `kind` is the type id of a built-in effect
(an instrument is refused: `track.set_instrument` replaces the instrument).
`index` is the position among the track's effects, 0 first (right after the
instrument); an index past the end means last. The new device starts at its
default settings, not bypassed. Refused with `invalid` when the effects around
that position share an order key (a merge made them equal), and with `limit` at the
safety limit of devices per track. Undo: `device.remove`.

Remove an effect from its track, with its settings. Refused for an instrument (the
oscillator, the clip player: replace it with `track.set_instrument`) and for a
device an automation lane targets. Undo: `device.restore` brings it back with its
identifier, position, settings and bypass.

Bring a removed effect back with its identifier, as `device.remove` took it out:
the inverse of a remove. `snapshot` is the whole device: its order key, bypass,
source, settings and state. Refused when the identifier is already in use, at the
safety limit of devices, or when the snapshot is not an effect (a built-in device
must be one of the registry, with only parameters it declares; a module device is
taken as it is) or does not fit the chain. Undo: `device.remove`.

Move an effect to `index` among its track's effects, 0 first (right after the
instrument); an index past the end means last. The instrument cannot be moved.
Refused with `invalid` when the effects around that position share an order key.
Undo: `device.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put an effect back under an exact order key: the inverse of `device.move`, which
takes an index. Refused when the key would put the effect before the instrument.
Undo: set the key before this command back.

Bypass a device (`bypass: true`: the chain skips it, its settings are kept) or put
it back (`false`). An instrument that is bypassed is silent. Refused for the clip
player of an audio track. Undo: set the previous state back.

Set a parameter of a device, by the parameter's id, in the unit the device
declares. The parameter must be one the device declares and the value must be
finite; it is clamped to the parameter's range and rounded to its step, and the
value stored (and returned) is the result. The built-in synth's parameters:
`waveform` (0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 triangle), `attack`, `decay` and
`release` (seconds, 0.002 to 30), `sustain` (0 to 1), `gain` (0 to 1, linear).
Every device's parameters (key, unit, range, default, and a `description` of what
each does) are in the device descriptors of the schema bundle. Undo: set the parameter back to its previous value.

DeviceId.description: Identifier of a device in a track's chain.

DeviceRole.description: What a device does in the chain.

DeviceSource.description: Where a device comes from. Third-party plugins come after the MVP.

oneOf.description: A device built into Faulk, by type id (`"faulk.osc_synth"`) and version.
A module of the Workshop, by name and the hash of its compiled code.

Edge.description: The edge of a placement that `arrangement.resize` moves.

oneOf.description:
The left edge: the end stays where it is, the placement shows the clip from
further on (or earlier).
The right edge: the start and the offset stay.
16-bit integers.
24-bit integers.
32-bit floats: nothing is clipped.

ExportRegion.description: Which part of the project is rendered.

oneOf.description: From the start to the end of the last placement of the arrangement, then the tail.
The loop region, once, then the tail.

From the start of bar `from_bar` to the end of bar `to_bar` (both counted from 1, the
second included), then the tail.

FrameLoop.description:
An audio clip's loop `[start, end)` in source frames, relative to the clip's start,
within `[0, frames]`.

Hash.description: The SHA-256 of a blob, 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

HistoryCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Undo the last entry of the history: one command, or every command of one
history group. Does nothing when there is nothing to undo; refused while a
group is open. Undo: `history.redo`.

Open a history group: every edit of the same author until `history.end_group`
becomes one entry, undone at once (a mouse drag). Refused when a group is
already open (groups do not nest). Undo and redo are refused while it is open:
the host ends it when the gesture or the turn ends. Not undoable itself.

Close the open history group. Refused when no group is open, or when another
author opened it. Not undoable itself.

Id.description: A stable identifier: 26 characters of Crockford base32 (a ULID), generated by the project.

LaunchCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Launch a MIDI clip of the launch grid at the next boundary of the launch
quantization; it replaces the clip its track plays. The clip must sit in a slot of
the grid (a clip of the arrangement only cannot be launched) and must not be an
audio clip (not launchable yet). If the transport is stopped, it starts playing
from its position, so the clip starts at the first boundary. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Launch every clip of a scene at the same boundary: each track plays the clip of its
slot in the scene, and a track whose slot is empty stops. An empty scene stops every
track that plays. If the transport is stopped, it starts playing from its position.
Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Stop the clip a track plays, or cancel the launch it waits for, at the next boundary
of the launch quantization. Does not start the transport. Played live: not undoable,
not saved.

Stop every track that plays a clip or waits for a launch, at the next boundary of
the launch quantization; it replaces the launches waiting. Does not start the
transport, and does not stop it. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Give every track back to its arrangement: a clip launched from the grid (or a stop
given from it) takes a track until this command. The notes of the grid's clips end
at once, launches still waiting for their boundary are dropped, and each track plays
its arrangement again from the playhead (a note already started on the timeline is
not restarted: it stays silent until its end). Does nothing to a track that follows
its arrangement. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Give one track back to its arrangement: what `launch.back_to_arrangement` does, for
the track alone; the other tracks are left as they are. Does nothing to a track that
follows its arrangement. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

LiveCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Start a note on a track's instrument. `note` is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127
(60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a note off. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.note_on` on the same track. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Play a note on the live input: it goes to the selected track and to every armed
MIDI track, as the session stands now (`view.select_track`, `track.arm`). `note`
is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127 (60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a
note off. Release it with `live.input_note_off`, which reaches the same tracks
whatever was selected or armed meanwhile. The output lists the tracks it went to.
Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.input_note_on`: on the tracks that note went
to, even if the selection or the arming changed since. Played live: not undoable,
not saved.

A control change (CC) on the live input, channels merged: `controller` 0 to 127,
`value` 0 to 127. It changes no sound by itself: it is reported to the interface
as a `control_change` event, for the automation (AM-5) to take. Controllers 120
(all sound off) and 123 (all notes off) are not sent here: hosts turn them into
`live.all_notes_off`. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Release every playing note on every track (panic button). Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

Cut every sound at once, on every track and the master: the output fades out in about
5 ms, then every instrument's voices (long releases included) and every effect's
tail (echo repeats, reverb) are cleared, without a click. The transport is not
touched. Use it when a sound rings on or feeds back out of control. Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

MidiCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
List the MIDI inputs available to the engine. The host answers with its
`midi.inputs` message: the inputs and the one selected.

Choose the MIDI input that plays the selected track. `id` is an id from
`midi.inputs`; `null` disconnects MIDI input. Session state: not undoable, not
saved with the project.

Mixer.description:
Gain, pan and mute of a track or of the master. Solo is not here: it is session state
(founder's decision 10). Sends come after the MVP.

gain_db.description: Gain in dB; `-inf` (silence) is written `null`.

MixerCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Set a track's volume in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value outside
the range or not a number is refused. A fader gesture sent in one history group
is undone in one step. Undo: set the previous volume back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Set a track's pan, from -1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside the range or
not a number is refused. A pan gesture sent in one history group is undone in
one step. Undo: set the previous pan back.

Mute or unmute a track. Mute is saved with the project and versioned. Undo: set
the previous state back.

Set the master's volume in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value
outside the range or not a number is refused. Undo: set the previous volume
back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

Note.description:
A note: a value without an id (CT-4). Its order compares fields in declaration order:
(start, pitch, length, velocity, cents, chance, repeat).

The last three fields are optional in the file: a default value is not written, and an
absent one reads as the default, so a note has exactly one representation. `chance` and
`repeat` are stored and edited here; the clip player reads them with #192.

cents.description: Fine tuning in cents, -50 to 50 (0 by default).

chance.description: Probability that the note plays, in percent, 0 to 100 (100 by default).

repeat.description: How many times the note repeats, 1 to 16 (1 by default).

start.description: Position from the start of the clip, in ticks.

NoteChange.description: A note to replace by another: `clip.notes.update` addresses a note by its whole value.

from.description: The note as it is in the clip now.

NoteCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

OrderKey.description: A fractional order key: elements sort by it.

Output.description: Where a track's signal goes. Only the master in the MVP; groups and returns later.

Placement.description: A clip set in the arrangement.

PlacementId.description: Identifier of a placement in a track's arrangement.

PlacementRecord.description: A placement of a clip as `arrangement.restore` writes it, with its identifier.

clip.description: A MIDI clip of the track.

length.description: Length on the timeline, in ticks.

offset.description: Where in the clip the placement starts, in ticks, before the clip's length.

start.description: Start in the arrangement, in ticks.

PlacementSnapshot.description:
A placement of a MIDI clip, with its identifier, as `clip.restore` brings it back. It
belongs to the clip restored: a snapshot cannot place another clip.

length.description: Length on the timeline, in ticks.

offset.description: Where in the clip the placement starts, in ticks, before the clip's length.

start.description: Start in the arrangement, in ticks.

ProjectCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Rename the project. The name is trimmed, not empty, at most 200 characters.
Undo: rename it back to its previous name.

Open the project folder the host staged under `folder` (the host reads the folder
first; named any other way, the command is refused as `not_staged`), replacing the
current project: the engine starts over from it (stopped, nothing held, the saved solo and
selection restored from `.faulk/session.json`). A folder that is not a valid
project of this version is refused with the reason and nothing changes. Replaces
the history: not undoable, destructive (the caller confirms first when the current
project has unsaved changes).

Start a new project: the page's default one, a single synth track, in no folder yet,
with its own identity. It replaces the current project, its history and its session
(the chosen MIDI input stays); the engine starts over from it. Not undoable, destructive:
the page first keeps the current project's changes where it can (written into its folder,
or kept as a draft in the browser's storage, which stays listed). Only when they cannot
be kept anywhere does it ask the user, whoever sends the command, and nothing changes if
the user cancels. The question is a dialog of the page, so it needs no click.

Write the project to its folder now, without waiting for the automatic save that
follows each change by a moment. A project that has no folder yet asks for one, as
`project.save_as` does. Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the
history.

Choose an empty folder and write the whole project into it; the project then lives
in that folder, and the automatic save keeps writing there. The folder is chosen by
the user (a browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by one gets
a notice in the page instead, and nothing is chosen. The old folder is left as it is. Changes nothing in the
project, so it never enters the history.

Export the project as a `.faulkpack`, a zip of its folder that any Faulk reads back,
and hand it to the user as a download. It holds the project as it is now, saved or
not, and the media the project refers to. This is how a project kept in the browser
(no folder chosen) is backed up or moved. Changes nothing in the project, so it never
enters the history.

Open a `.faulkpack` the user chooses: its project replaces the current one and is kept
in the browser as a new project of its own (an import never overwrites a project that
is already there). A file is chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so
an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the page instead. A file that is
not a valid pack is refused with the reason and nothing changes. The history of the
replaced project is gone; the page asks first when that project has changes that are
not kept anywhere.

List the projects this page can open: the folders opened recently (each with an `id`)
and the projects kept in the browser's own storage (each with a `dir`), newest first.
The page reads its storage again before it answers. The `id` and the `dir` are the
names `project.open_recent`, `project.open_browser_project` and
`project.delete_browser_project` take. Changes nothing in the project.

Bring back the project that was open last time, the one the page offers after a reload
(a folder, which asks the browser for its permission again and so needs a click by the
user, or a draft kept in the browser). Nothing happens, with a notice, when the page
offers nothing. The current project is replaced; the page asks first when it has
changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Choose a project folder and open it, replacing the current project. The folder is
chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by
one gets a notice in the page instead. A folder that is not a project is refused with
the reason and nothing changes. The page asks first when the current project has
changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Open a folder from the recent projects, by the `id` that `project.list_stored` gives,
replacing the current project. When the browser withdrew its permission on the folder,
it asks again, which needs a click by the user: an agent that is not driven by one gets
a notice in the page. An `id` the page does not know is refused with a notice. The page
asks first when the current project has changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it
replaces the history.

Open a project kept in the browser's storage (a draft, or a project where the browser
has no folders), by the `dir` that `project.list_stored` gives, replacing the current
project. A `dir` the page does not list is refused with a notice, and so is a project
that another tab has open. The page asks first when the current project has changes
that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Delete a project kept in the browser's storage, for good, by the `dir` that
`project.list_stored` gives. The page always asks the user to confirm first, whoever
sends the command, and nothing is deleted until the user says yes. The project that is
open, a project another tab has open and a `dir` the page does not list are refused
with a notice. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user
answered. Not undoable: the files are gone (`project.export_pack` makes a copy first).

When the project's folder was edited outside Faulk while the project has unsaved
changes, keep this page's version: the folder's files are replaced by the project right
away, and the outside edits are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

When the project's folder was edited outside Faulk while the project has unsaved
changes, take the folder's version: the project is replaced by what the folder holds,
and the changes made since the last write are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Not undoable: it replaces the history.

After the browser withdrew the right to write in the project's folder, ask for it
again (the browser shows a prompt, which needs a click by the user: an agent that is
not driven by one gets a notice in the page), then write the changes that waited.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

Render the project to an audio file (WAV) and save it, offline: the same engine
that plays the song, run faster than real time, so the file is the song as it
sounds, not a recording of the speakers. `region` is `song` (default: from bar 1
to the end of the last placement of the arrangement, then the tail, so that an
effect such as the echo rings out; the file ends where the sound falls under
-90 dBFS, after 30 seconds at most), `loop` (the loop region once, then the same
tail) or `bars` (from the start of bar `from_bar` to the end of bar `to_bar`, both
counted from 1, required with it and refused without it, the last one included,
then the same tail). `bit_depth` is `pcm16`, `pcm24` (default) or `float32`;
`sample_rate` is 44100, 48000 (default) or 96000. The metronome is never in the
file; the solo and mute state are. It is refused when there is nothing to render
(empty arrangement, no loop region for `loop`, a `bars` range that starts after the
end of the arrangement or is out of order) or the range lasts more than 30 minutes
(a `limit` error). The output says what will be rendered; the page runs the render, shows its progress and asks
where to save the file (a folder picker needs a click), so an agent that is not
driven by a user gets the render in the page to confirm. Changes nothing in the
project, so it never enters the history and has nothing to undo.

Quantize.description:
The launch quantization: the grid a launch snaps to. Global to the project at the MVP,
one bar by default (founder's decision 8).

The grid is anchored at tick 0; [`Quantize::Sixteenth`] is a sixteenth note whatever
the signature, [`Quantize::Beat`] and the bars follow the [`TimeSignature`].

oneOf.description: No quantization: a launch happens at once.
A sixteenth note (240 ticks).
One beat of the time signature.
One bar.
Two bars.
Four bars.
Eight bars.

RecordCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

SceneClip.description:
A clip of a deleted scene, with its identifier, its track and its placements in the
arrangement, as `scene.restore` brings it back. MIDI or audio: it is the clip as the
project holds it.

placements.description: Its placements, by identifier.

SceneCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Create a scene at the end of the launch grid. `name` is optional (trimmed, at most
200 characters; empty by default). The new scene's slots are empty. Refused with
`limit` only at the project's safety limit of scenes. Undo: `scene.delete`.

Delete a scene with the clips of its launch-grid slots, and their placements in the
arrangement. Not destructive: undo brings everything back. A clip that is playing
stops sounding when its notes are released. Undo: `scene.restore` brings the scene
and its clips back with their identifiers and position.

Bring a deleted scene back with its identifier, its name, its position and the
clips of its slots, as `scene.delete` removed it: the inverse of a delete. Refused
when the scene's identifier or any identifier inside it is already in use, at the
safety limit of scenes, when a clip's slot is not this scene or two clips share a
track, or when the snapshot is not a valid project. Undo: `scene.delete`.

Rename a scene. The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an empty name clears
it. Undo: rename it back.

Move a scene to `index` in the list of scenes, 0 first; an index past the end
means last. Refused with `invalid` when the scenes around that position share an
order key (a merge made them equal), since none fits between them. Undo:
`scene.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put a scene back under an exact order key: the inverse of `scene.move`, which takes
an index. Undo: set the key before this command back.

ScenePlacement.description: A placement of a clip of a deleted scene, with its identifier.

SceneSnapshot.description: A scene as `scene.restore` brings it back (everything but its identifier).

Shape.description: The shape of the transition from a point to the next one.

Span.description:
The extent of a placement: in ticks for a MIDI clip, in source frames for an audio
clip.

Tick.description:
A musical position or duration, in ticks ([`PPQ`] per quarter note).

Arithmetic saturates instead of overflowing. The inner value is public so that the
project and the UI read it as a plain integer.

TickLoop.description: A MIDI clip's loop `[start, end)` in ticks, within `[0, length]`.

Track.description: A track: its chain of devices, its clips, its arrangement and its automation.

devices.description:
The chain: at most one instrument, first, then effects, ordered by
[`Device::order`].

placements.description: This track's arrangement.

TrackCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Create a track at the end of the list: `kind` is `midi` or `audio`. A MIDI track
plays `instrument`, the type id of a built-in instrument (`faulk.osc_synth`, the
default); an audio track plays the clip player and takes no `instrument`. `name`
is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters; empty by default) and so is `color`
(`#rrggbb`). Refused with `limit` only at the project's safety limit of tracks.
Undo: `track.delete`.

Delete a track with its devices, clips, placements and automation. The selection,
the solo, the arming and the monitoring of the track are cleared (session state,
not restored by undo: an undone delete brings the track back unarmed). Undo:
`track.restore` brings the whole track back with its identifiers and position.

Bring a deleted track back with its identifier, as `track.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. `snapshot` is the whole track: its order key, mixer,
devices, clips, placements and automation. Refused when the track's identifier or
any identifier inside it is already in use, at the safety limit of tracks, or when
the snapshot is not a valid track of the project. Undo: `track.delete`.

Rename a track. The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an empty name clears
it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the colour of a track, `#rrggbb`, or `null` for none. Undo: set the previous
colour back.

color.description: Required: `null` clears the colour, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Move a track to `index` in the list of tracks, 0 first; an index past the end
means last. Refused with `invalid` when the tracks around that position share an
order key (a merge made them equal), since none fits between them. Undo: `track.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put a track back under an exact order key: the inverse of `track.move`, which
takes an index. Refused when the key is not a valid order key (checked on read).
Undo: set the key before this command back.

Replace a MIDI track's instrument by another instrument of the registry: `instrument`
is the type id of a built-in instrument (`faulk.osc_synth`, `faulk.drums`). The new
device starts at its default settings under a new identifier and takes the old
one's place first in the chain; the effects stay. The old instrument's settings are
lost unless undone. Choosing the instrument the track already plays changes
nothing. Refused on an audio track (it plays the clip player), for a type that is
not an instrument, and when an automation lane targets the old instrument. Undo:
`track.restore_instrument` brings the old instrument back with its identifier and
settings.

Swap a track's instrument for a device taken out earlier: the inverse of
`track.set_instrument`. `current` is the instrument in the track now, replaced by
`snapshot` under the identifier `device`. Refused when `device` is already in use,
when `current` is not the track's instrument, when an automation lane targets it,
or when the snapshot is not an instrument that fits the track (a built-in device
must be one of the registry; a module device is taken as it is). Undo: the same
swap the other way.

Arm or disarm a track: live input (`live.input_note_on`, the keyboard and MIDI
controllers) reaches the armed tracks as well as the selected one, and recording
captures them. Session state: not undoable, not in the history, not saved with
the project. Refused with `not_found` for a track that does not exist, except to
disarm a track deleted since.

Monitor or stop monitoring a track's live input through its chain. Session
state: not undoable, not in the history, not saved with the project. A MIDI
track's instrument sounds what is played whatever this says; it matters for the
audio input. Refused with `not_found` for a track that does not exist, except to
stop monitoring a track deleted since.

Duplicate a track right after the source (after any track that shares its order
key), with new identifiers for the track, its
devices, clips, placements and automation lanes. The clips are new, independent
clips with the same content, each with the next name ("Clip 2" gives "Clip 3").
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200
characters): the copy has the source's name by default. The copy is never muted
(volume and pan are copied); solo and arming are session state of the source and
are not copied. Refused with `limit` at
the safety limit of tracks, notes or automation points. Undo: `track.delete` of
the copy.

clips.description: Clips to bring back (their identifiers must be unused).

put.description:
Placements to write exactly as given: created, or replaced when the identifier
is already a placement of the track.

remove.description: Placements of the track to remove.

remove_clips.description: Clips of the track to remove; no placement may be left on them.

oneOf.description: MIDI clips, played by the track's instrument.
Audio clips, played by the clip player ([`CLIP_PLAYER`]).

TransportCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Start playback from the position of the last `transport.seek` (the start of the
project at first), also after a `transport.stop`. Does nothing while already
playing. Played live: not undoable, not saved.
Stop playback. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Move the playhead to `tick` (960 ticks per quarter note), from 0 to 2^40. Played
live: not undoable, not saved.

Set the project's tempo in BPM, from 20 to 999. A value outside the range or not
a number is refused. Undo: set the previous tempo back.

Set the project's time signature: numerator 1 to 32, denominator a power of two
from 1 to 32 (4 and 4 is common time). Anything else is refused. Undo: set the
previous signature back.

Set the launch quantization, global to the project: the grid a clip or scene launch
snaps to. One of `none` (at once), `sixteenth`, `beat`, `bar`, `bars_2`, `bars_4`,
`bars_8`; a project starts at `bar`. Any other value is refused. Undo: set the
previous value back.

Set the loop region `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with `0 <= start < end <=
2^40`, or `null` for none; a region cannot be cleared while the loop is on. This
does not turn the loop on: see `transport.toggle_loop`. Undo: set the previous
region back.

Turn the loop over the loop region on or off. Turning it on without a region is
refused. Undo: toggle again.

Change the metronome: `enabled` (click on or off), `gain_db` (level, -96 to +6,
`null` for silence) and `count_in_bars` (bars counted in before recording, 0 to 16). Every field is
optional and a missing one is left as it is; at least one is required. A value
outside its range is refused. Undo: set the previous values of the changed fields
back.

gain_db.description: The level in dB; `null` is silence; missing leaves it as it is.

catalog.description:
Split a placement in two at the timeline tick `at`, strictly inside it: the left
part keeps the identifier, the right part is a new placement (the same clip, so
linked) that plays on from where the left one stops. Refused when the clip has
nothing left to play at `at` (a clip without a loop that ended before). Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

ArrangementCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Put a MIDI clip of the arrangement again in the arrangement, as a new placement of
the same clip (a linked clip: editing the clip changes every placement of it). A
clip that sits in the launch grid is refused: copying or linking it is
`arrangement.place_from_slot`. `start` is in
ticks; `offset` (default 0, before the clip's length) is where in the clip the
placement starts; `length` (default: what is left of the clip after `offset`) is
its length on the timeline, which may exceed the clip (a clip with a loop repeats
it, one without is silent after its end). The new placement wins on overlap: the
other placements of the track that it covers are removed, shortened, trimmed at
the front or split (`overwritten` counts them). Undo: `arrangement.restore`.

Move placements in time, all by the same number of ticks (`by`, negative moves
them earlier), in one command: a drag of a selection is one history entry. Each
placement stays in its own track and keeps its length and offset. The moved
placements win on overlap (the placements of the track that they cover are
carved, `overwritten` counts them); they may move onto each other's old place.
Refused when one would start before tick 0 or end past 2^40, or when the list is
empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one. A move by 0 changes nothing.
Undo: `arrangement.restore`.

Move one edge of a placement to the timeline tick `to`. `edge: "end"` changes the
length (the end must stay after the start); `edge: "start"` moves the start with
the end fixed, and the offset follows so the content does not slide: shortening
from the left cuts the beginning of the clip (through the clip's loop), growing to
the left shows earlier content and is refused beyond the clip's start (offset 0).
The resized placement wins on overlap (the others it now covers are carved,
`overwritten` counts them). Moving the edge where it is changes nothing. Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

Split a placement in two at the timeline tick `at`, strictly inside it: the left
part keeps the identifier, the right part is a new placement (the same clip, so
linked) that plays on from where the left one stops. Refused when the clip has
nothing left to play at `at` (a clip without a loop that ended before). Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

Delete placements, in one command. A clip that sits in the launch grid or has
other placements stays; a clip of the arrangement only that loses its last
placement is deleted with it (the undo brings it back with its notes). Refused when the
list is empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one. Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

Copy placements, in one command. The copies start `by` ticks after the originals
(default: right after the selection, one selection length later; negative copies
earlier). By default each copy is independent: a new clip, a copy of the source
(the next name, "Clip 2" gives "Clip 3"; same colour, length, loop and notes; not
in the launch grid), one per
distinct source clip, so placements that were linked stay linked among the copies
and editing a copy never changes the original (founder's decision 11). With
`linked: true` the copies are new placements of the same clips. The copies win
on overlap (`overwritten` counts the placements they carved). Refused when the
list is empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one, or when a copy would
leave the timeline. Undo: `arrangement.restore`, which removes the copies and
the clips created.

Put a MIDI clip of the launch grid in the arrangement, on its own track, as a
placement at the timeline tick `start` that plays the whole clip once (offset 0,
the clip's length). By default the placement plays an independent copy: a new
clip, a copy of the grid clip (the next name like `clip.duplicate`, "Clip 2" gives "Clip 3"; same colour, length, loop and notes, not in
the launch grid), so editing one never changes the other (founder's decision 11).
With `linked: true` the placement references the grid clip itself: editing the
clip in the grid changes what the arrangement plays. The placement wins on overlap
(`overwritten` counts the placements it carved). Refused for a clip that is not in
the launch grid (use `arrangement.place` or `arrangement.duplicate`), for an audio
clip, or when the clip would leave the timeline. Undo: `arrangement.restore`,
which removes the placement and the copy.

`arrangement.place_from_slot` for a whole scene of the launch grid, in one command
and one history entry: every MIDI clip of the scene is placed on its own track at
the same tick `start`, as a copy (default) or linked to the grid clip. Empty slots
place nothing; audio clips are skipped. Refused when the scene has no MIDI clip.
The placements win on overlap. Undo: `arrangement.restore`.

Write the placements of one or more tracks exactly as given, without the overlap
rule: the inverse of every arrangement command, which brings back what it carved,
with the identifiers. Per track: `put` creates or replaces placements by
identifier, `remove` removes placements, `clips` brings back MIDI clips (new
identifiers, a snapshot as `clip.restore` takes) and `remove_clips` removes clips.
Refused when a placement is outside the timeline or its offset outside its clip,
when a placement is left on a removed clip or names an unknown clip, when an
identifier to create is in use, or when a rule of the clip commands is broken (a
note outside the length, a limit). Undo: the restore of what it changed.

ClipCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters): without one the clip gets the
next default name, "Clip n" with n the first number no clip of the project has; it
is stored and never changes when other clips move, are copied or deleted. Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Delete a MIDI clip and its placements in the arrangement. Undo: `clip.restore`
brings back the clip, its notes and its placements with their identifiers.

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip: the next name ("Clip 2" gives
"Clip 3", the first number not taken in the project; "Bass" gives "Bass 2"), same
colour, length, loop and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot: of the source's track, or of `track` when given (another MIDI
track). `slot` when given must be free in that track, otherwise the copy takes
the first free slot (below the source's scene in the same track, from the top in
another). Refused, with no effect, when the track has no free slot to give. A
second placement of the same clip is an option of the arrangement commands, not
of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of the copy.

Move a MIDI clip to another launch-grid slot, of the same track or of `track`
(another MIDI track), keeping its identifier, its name and its content. `slot`
is the scene of the target slot, which must be free; `null` takes the clip out of
the grid, which is refused when no placement of the arrangement plays it. A clip
that has placements stays in its track: moving it to another track is refused.
A move that changes nothing does nothing and leaves no history entry. Leaving
`slot` out is the same as `null`. The engine frees the clip and takes it again, so
a clip that is playing stops, and so does the arrangement's playback of its
placements (they play again from the next note). Undo: move it back.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name gives a MIDI clip the next default name ("Clip n"; one that already has a
default name keeps it) and clears an audio clip's. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Every placement of the clip that plays it
whole (offset 0, length equal to the old length of the clip) takes the new length
in the same command, so notes added past the old end are heard in the
arrangement; a growing placement stops at the start of the next placement of its
track, and a placement that shows only part of the clip, or repeats it, is left
alone. Undo: set the length back, restoring what `trim` cut and the lengths of the
placements.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused), and the placements follow the length in the same way
as `clip.set_length`. Undo: set the previous content and the previous placement
lengths back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

Quantize the start of notes of a MIDI clip toward a grid, in one batch (one history
entry, all or nothing). `grid` is the grid step in ticks (960 per quarter note, at
least 1); `strength` is 0 to 100 percent: 100 puts a note on the nearest grid line
(halfway goes to the later line), 50 moves it half of the way, 0 changes nothing.
`notes` lists the notes to quantize, each by its whole value; leave it out to
quantize every note of the clip. A listed note that is not in the clip is refused.
Only the start moves: the length never changes. A note that the move would push past
the end of the clip stops where it still fits (its end on the clip's end), so it may
be off the grid. Notes that end up equal merge into one. Undo: the opposite moves
(the previous content of the clip when notes merged).

Transpose notes of a MIDI clip by `semitones` (positive up, negative down), in one
batch (one history entry, all or nothing). Each note is addressed by its whole
value and must be in the clip. A transposition that would take one note outside
pitch 0 to 127 is refused for the whole batch, never clamped. Notes that end up
equal merge into one. 0 semitones changes nothing. Undo: transpose back (the
previous content of the clip when notes merged).

Copy notes of a MIDI clip, shifted in time by `offset` ticks (negative: earlier), in
one batch (one history entry, all or nothing). Each source note is addressed by its
whole value and must be in the clip. Without `offset`, the copies follow the whole
selection (shift of the span from the first start to the last end). An `offset` of 0
is refused, and so is a copy that would lie outside `[0, clip length]` (never
truncated). A copy equal to a note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo: remove
the notes actually added.
Musical time: length and loop in ticks.

Source time: a range `[start, start + frames)` of an audio file, in frames. No
length in ticks is stored: it is computed at the project's tempo.

DeviceCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Insert an effect in a track's chain. `kind` is the type id of a built-in effect
(an instrument is refused: `track.set_instrument` replaces the instrument).
`index` is the position among the track's effects, 0 first (right after the
instrument); an index past the end means last. The new device starts at its
default settings, not bypassed. Refused with `invalid` when the effects around
that position share an order key (a merge made them equal), and with `limit` at the
safety limit of devices per track. Undo: `device.remove`.

Remove an effect from its track, with its settings. Refused for an instrument (the
oscillator, the clip player: replace it with `track.set_instrument`) and for a
device an automation lane targets. Undo: `device.restore` brings it back with its
identifier, position, settings and bypass.

Bring a removed effect back with its identifier, as `device.remove` took it out:
the inverse of a remove. `snapshot` is the whole device: its order key, bypass,
source, settings and state. Refused when the identifier is already in use, at the
safety limit of devices, or when the snapshot is not an effect (a built-in device
must be one of the registry, with only parameters it declares; a module device is
taken as it is) or does not fit the chain. Undo: `device.remove`.

Move an effect to `index` among its track's effects, 0 first (right after the
instrument); an index past the end means last. The instrument cannot be moved.
Refused with `invalid` when the effects around that position share an order key.
Undo: `device.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put an effect back under an exact order key: the inverse of `device.move`, which
takes an index. Refused when the key would put the effect before the instrument.
Undo: set the key before this command back.

Bypass a device (`bypass: true`: the chain skips it, its settings are kept) or put
it back (`false`). An instrument that is bypassed is silent. Refused for the clip
player of an audio track. Undo: set the previous state back.

Set a parameter of a device, by the parameter's id, in the unit the device
declares. The parameter must be one the device declares and the value must be
finite; it is clamped to the parameter's range and rounded to its step, and the
value stored (and returned) is the result. The built-in synth's parameters:
`waveform` (0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 triangle), `attack`, `decay` and
`release` (seconds, 0.002 to 30), `sustain` (0 to 1), `gain` (0 to 1, linear).
Every device's parameters (key, unit, range, default, and a `description` of what
each does) are in the device descriptors of the schema bundle. Undo: set the parameter back to its previous value.

HistoryCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Undo the last entry of the history: one command, or every command of one
history group. Does nothing when there is nothing to undo; refused while a
group is open. Undo: `history.redo`.

Open a history group: every edit of the same author until `history.end_group`
becomes one entry, undone at once (a mouse drag). Refused when a group is
already open (groups do not nest). Undo and redo are refused while it is open:
the host ends it when the gesture or the turn ends. Not undoable itself.

Close the open history group. Refused when no group is open, or when another
author opened it. Not undoable itself.

LaunchCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Launch a MIDI clip of the launch grid at the next boundary of the launch
quantization; it replaces the clip its track plays. The clip must sit in a slot of
the grid (a clip of the arrangement only cannot be launched) and must not be an
audio clip (not launchable yet). If the transport is stopped, it starts playing
from its position, so the clip starts at the first boundary. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Launch every clip of a scene at the same boundary: each track plays the clip of its
slot in the scene, and a track whose slot is empty stops. An empty scene stops every
track that plays. If the transport is stopped, it starts playing from its position.
Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Stop the clip a track plays, or cancel the launch it waits for, at the next boundary
of the launch quantization. Does not start the transport. Played live: not undoable,
not saved.

Stop every track that plays a clip or waits for a launch, at the next boundary of
the launch quantization; it replaces the launches waiting. Does not start the
transport, and does not stop it. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Give every track back to its arrangement: a clip launched from the grid (or a stop
given from it) takes a track until this command. The notes of the grid's clips end
at once, launches still waiting for their boundary are dropped, and each track plays
its arrangement again from the playhead (a note already started on the timeline is
not restarted: it stays silent until its end). Does nothing to a track that follows
its arrangement. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Give one track back to its arrangement: what `launch.back_to_arrangement` does, for
the track alone; the other tracks are left as they are. Does nothing to a track that
follows its arrangement. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

LiveCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Start a note on a track's instrument. `note` is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127
(60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a note off. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.note_on` on the same track. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Play a note on the live input: it goes to the selected track and to every armed
MIDI track, as the session stands now (`view.select_track`, `track.arm`). `note`
is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127 (60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a
note off. Release it with `live.input_note_off`, which reaches the same tracks
whatever was selected or armed meanwhile. The output lists the tracks it went to.
Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.input_note_on`: on the tracks that note went
to, even if the selection or the arming changed since. Played live: not undoable,
not saved.

A control change (CC) on the live input, channels merged: `controller` 0 to 127,
`value` 0 to 127. It changes no sound by itself: it is reported to the interface
as a `control_change` event, for the automation (AM-5) to take. Controllers 120
(all sound off) and 123 (all notes off) are not sent here: hosts turn them into
`live.all_notes_off`. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Release every playing note on every track (panic button). Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

Cut every sound at once, on every track and the master: the output fades out in about
5 ms, then every instrument's voices (long releases included) and every effect's
tail (echo repeats, reverb) are cleared, without a click. The transport is not
touched. Use it when a sound rings on or feeds back out of control. Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

`repeat` are stored and edited here; the clip player reads them with #192.

ProjectCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Rename the project. The name is trimmed, not empty, at most 200 characters.
Undo: rename it back to its previous name.

Open the project folder the host staged under `folder` (the host reads the folder
first; named any other way, the command is refused as `not_staged`), replacing the
current project: the engine starts over from it (stopped, nothing held, the saved solo and
selection restored from `.faulk/session.json`). A folder that is not a valid
project of this version is refused with the reason and nothing changes. Replaces
the history: not undoable, destructive (the caller confirms first when the current
project has unsaved changes).

Start a new project: the page's default one, a single synth track, in no folder yet,
with its own identity. It replaces the current project, its history and its session
(the chosen MIDI input stays); the engine starts over from it. Not undoable, destructive:
the page first keeps the current project's changes where it can (written into its folder,
or kept as a draft in the browser's storage, which stays listed). Only when they cannot
be kept anywhere does it ask the user, whoever sends the command, and nothing changes if
the user cancels. The question is a dialog of the page, so it needs no click.

Write the project to its folder now, without waiting for the automatic save that
follows each change by a moment. A project that has no folder yet asks for one, as
`project.save_as` does. Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the
history.

Choose an empty folder and write the whole project into it; the project then lives
in that folder, and the automatic save keeps writing there. The folder is chosen by
the user (a browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by one gets
a notice in the page instead, and nothing is chosen. The old folder is left as it is. Changes nothing in the
project, so it never enters the history.

Export the project as a `.faulkpack`, a zip of its folder that any Faulk reads back,
and hand it to the user as a download. It holds the project as it is now, saved or
not, and the media the project refers to. This is how a project kept in the browser
(no folder chosen) is backed up or moved. Changes nothing in the project, so it never
enters the history.

Open a `.faulkpack` the user chooses: its project replaces the current one and is kept
in the browser as a new project of its own (an import never overwrites a project that
is already there). A file is chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so
an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the page instead. A file that is
not a valid pack is refused with the reason and nothing changes. The history of the
replaced project is gone; the page asks first when that project has changes that are
not kept anywhere.

List the projects this page can open: the folders opened recently (each with an `id`)
and the projects kept in the browser's own storage (each with a `dir`), newest first.
The page reads its storage again before it answers. The `id` and the `dir` are the
names `project.open_recent`, `project.open_browser_project` and
`project.delete_browser_project` take. Changes nothing in the project.

Bring back the project that was open last time, the one the page offers after a reload
(a folder, which asks the browser for its permission again and so needs a click by the
user, or a draft kept in the browser). Nothing happens, with a notice, when the page
offers nothing. The current project is replaced; the page asks first when it has
changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Choose a project folder and open it, replacing the current project. The folder is
chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by
one gets a notice in the page instead. A folder that is not a project is refused with
the reason and nothing changes. The page asks first when the current project has
changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Open a folder from the recent projects, by the `id` that `project.list_stored` gives,
replacing the current project. When the browser withdrew its permission on the folder,
it asks again, which needs a click by the user: an agent that is not driven by one gets
a notice in the page. An `id` the page does not know is refused with a notice. The page
asks first when the current project has changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it
replaces the history.

Open a project kept in the browser's storage (a draft, or a project where the browser
has no folders), by the `dir` that `project.list_stored` gives, replacing the current
project. A `dir` the page does not list is refused with a notice, and so is a project
that another tab has open. The page asks first when the current project has changes
that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Delete a project kept in the browser's storage, for good, by the `dir` that
`project.list_stored` gives. The page always asks the user to confirm first, whoever
sends the command, and nothing is deleted until the user says yes. The project that is
open, a project another tab has open and a `dir` the page does not list are refused
with a notice. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user
answered. Not undoable: the files are gone (`project.export_pack` makes a copy first).

When the project's folder was edited outside Faulk while the project has unsaved
changes, keep this page's version: the folder's files are replaced by the project right
away, and the outside edits are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

When the project's folder was edited outside Faulk while the project has unsaved
changes, take the folder's version: the project is replaced by what the folder holds,
and the changes made since the last write are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Not undoable: it replaces the history.

After the browser withdrew the right to write in the project's folder, ask for it
again (the browser shows a prompt, which needs a click by the user: an agent that is
not driven by one gets a notice in the page), then write the changes that waited.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

Render the project to an audio file (WAV) and save it, offline: the same engine
that plays the song, run faster than real time, so the file is the song as it
sounds, not a recording of the speakers. `region` is `song` (default: from bar 1
to the end of the last placement of the arrangement, then the tail, so that an
effect such as the echo rings out; the file ends where the sound falls under
-90 dBFS, after 30 seconds at most), `loop` (the loop region once, then the same
tail) or `bars` (from the start of bar `from_bar` to the end of bar `to_bar`, both
counted from 1, required with it and refused without it, the last one included,
then the same tail). `bit_depth` is `pcm16`, `pcm24` (default) or `float32`;
`sample_rate` is 44100, 48000 (default) or 96000. The metronome is never in the
file; the solo and mute state are. It is refused when there is nothing to render
(empty arrangement, no loop region for `loop`, a `bars` range that starts after the
end of the arrangement or is out of order) or the range lasts more than 30 minutes
(a `limit` error). The output says what will be rendered; the page runs the render, shows its progress and asks
where to save the file (a folder picker needs a click), so an agent that is not
driven by a user gets the render in the page to confirm. Changes nothing in the
project, so it never enters the history and has nothing to undo.

oneOf.description:
Create a scene at the end of the launch grid. `name` is optional (trimmed, at most
200 characters; empty by default). The new scene's slots are empty. Refused with
`limit` only at the project's safety limit of scenes. Undo: `scene.delete`.

Delete a scene with the clips of its launch-grid slots, and their placements in the
arrangement. Not destructive: undo brings everything back. A clip that is playing
stops sounding when its notes are released. Undo: `scene.restore` brings the scene
and its clips back with their identifiers and position.

Bring a deleted scene back with its identifier, its name, its position and the
clips of its slots, as `scene.delete` removed it: the inverse of a delete. Refused
when the scene's identifier or any identifier inside it is already in use, at the
safety limit of scenes, when a clip's slot is not this scene or two clips share a
track, or when the snapshot is not a valid project. Undo: `scene.delete`.

Rename a scene. The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an empty name clears
it. Undo: rename it back.

Move a scene to `index` in the list of scenes, 0 first; an index past the end
means last. Refused with `invalid` when the scenes around that position share an
order key (a merge made them equal), since none fits between them. Undo:
`scene.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put a scene back under an exact order key: the inverse of `scene.move`, which takes
an index. Undo: set the key before this command back.

TrackCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Create a track at the end of the list: `kind` is `midi` or `audio`. A MIDI track
plays `instrument`, the type id of a built-in instrument (`faulk.osc_synth`, the
default); an audio track plays the clip player and takes no `instrument`. `name`
is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters; empty by default) and so is `color`
(`#rrggbb`). Refused with `limit` only at the project's safety limit of tracks.
Undo: `track.delete`.

Delete a track with its devices, clips, placements and automation. The selection,
the solo, the arming and the monitoring of the track are cleared (session state,
not restored by undo: an undone delete brings the track back unarmed). Undo:
`track.restore` brings the whole track back with its identifiers and position.

Bring a deleted track back with its identifier, as `track.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. `snapshot` is the whole track: its order key, mixer,
devices, clips, placements and automation. Refused when the track's identifier or
any identifier inside it is already in use, at the safety limit of tracks, or when
the snapshot is not a valid track of the project. Undo: `track.delete`.

Rename a track. The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an empty name clears
it. Undo: rename it back.

Set the colour of a track, `#rrggbb`, or `null` for none. Undo: set the previous
colour back.

color.description: Required: `null` clears the colour, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Move a track to `index` in the list of tracks, 0 first; an index past the end
means last. Refused with `invalid` when the tracks around that position share an
order key (a merge made them equal), since none fits between them. Undo: `track.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put a track back under an exact order key: the inverse of `track.move`, which
takes an index. Refused when the key is not a valid order key (checked on read).
Undo: set the key before this command back.

Replace a MIDI track's instrument by another instrument of the registry: `instrument`
is the type id of a built-in instrument (`faulk.osc_synth`, `faulk.drums`). The new
device starts at its default settings under a new identifier and takes the old
one's place first in the chain; the effects stay. The old instrument's settings are
lost unless undone. Choosing the instrument the track already plays changes
nothing. Refused on an audio track (it plays the clip player), for a type that is
not an instrument, and when an automation lane targets the old instrument. Undo:
`track.restore_instrument` brings the old instrument back with its identifier and
settings.

Swap a track's instrument for a device taken out earlier: the inverse of
`track.set_instrument`. `current` is the instrument in the track now, replaced by
`snapshot` under the identifier `device`. Refused when `device` is already in use,
when `current` is not the track's instrument, when an automation lane targets it,
or when the snapshot is not an instrument that fits the track (a built-in device
must be one of the registry; a module device is taken as it is). Undo: the same
swap the other way.

Arm or disarm a track: live input (`live.input_note_on`, the keyboard and MIDI
controllers) reaches the armed tracks as well as the selected one, and recording
captures them. Session state: not undoable, not in the history, not saved with
the project. Refused with `not_found` for a track that does not exist, except to
disarm a track deleted since.

Monitor or stop monitoring a track's live input through its chain. Session
state: not undoable, not in the history, not saved with the project. A MIDI
track's instrument sounds what is played whatever this says; it matters for the
audio input. Refused with `not_found` for a track that does not exist, except to
stop monitoring a track deleted since.

Duplicate a track right after the source (after any track that shares its order
key), with new identifiers for the track, its
devices, clips, placements and automation lanes. The clips are new, independent
clips with the same content, each with the next name ("Clip 2" gives "Clip 3").
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200
characters): the copy has the source's name by default. The copy is never muted
(volume and pan are copied); solo and arming are session state of the source and
are not copied. Refused with `limit` at
the safety limit of tracks, notes or automation points. Undo: `track.delete` of
the copy.
